purpose: Teach: 毛沢東/ホークス/バーゲン/ダービー/ペナルティ/ガンバ/レーガン/プリンス

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが毛沢東主義の本を読まれた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to read books about Mao and communism.
lines.style: Soft, distant gaze into memory. Opening word gentle and searching. Pace unhurried, as if watching a scene from decades away. Breath steady but tender — not sad, just... far.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、ホークスの試合をテレビで観られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and your grandfather watched the Hawks game on television, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm acknowledgment with a gentle redirect. A patient smile in the voice. Tender but slightly teasing — she knows where his mind goes, lets him wander, brings him back with affection.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、デパートのバーゲンに並んだのよ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, I remember standing in those long lines at the department store sales.
lines.style: Quieter now, more intimate. A small smile threading through. Pace slower, savoring the particular texture of that memory — crowded, eager, alive in a way only youth allows.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、英国ダービーをラジオでお聴きになったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And your grandfather listened to the English Derby on the radio, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Playful but insistent. A gentle push — she's steering him back, but with warmth, not correction. Light touch on 'didn't he' like she's asking him to stay present with her.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがサッカーのペナルティの解説をされた
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, my father used to explain soccer penalty kicks to me so carefully.
lines.style: Voice catches slightly on the memory of his father's voice. Grateful, reverent. Slow unfolding of the image. Trailing off on the image itself — the detail of his father's attention.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ガンバの試合に行かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you went to see Gamba play, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Knows the answer already. Not questioning — confirming, gently insisting he stay tethered to their shared story. Warm but with an undercurrent of 'I'm here, stay with me.'

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがレーガン時代の経済の本を読まれた
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, my father read those thick books about the Reagan era and economics.
lines.style: Voice steadies on the intellectual memory. A note of admiration beneath. Pace deliberate — these details matter to him, even now. Slight lift on 'Reagan era' as if it conjures an entire world.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、プリンスホテルでお祝いされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And we had that celebration at the Prince Hotel, didn't we, dear?
lines.style: Softest landing of all. Almost a whisper now. Not pulling him back this time — settling into the memory with him. Tender, tired, complete. The voice of someone who knows time is short and wants him to know she was there too.
